title: Parity of the functional-equation exponent
statement:
Let $p$ be prime, let $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, put $q=p^a$ and
$k_0=\Fq$, and let $k=\Fbar$ be the fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$.
Fix an indeterminate $T$. Let $X_0/k_0$ be smooth, proper, and
geometrically connected of pure dimension $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, and
put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. For every prime $\ell\neq p$, write
$\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, for $P(T)=\sum_r c_rT^r\in\mathbf Z[T]$ write
$P^{(\ell)}(T)=\sum_r(c_r\cdot1_{\Ql})T^r$, let
$(V_{i,\ell},F_{i,\ell},P_{i,\ell})_{0\leq i\leq2d}$ be the
smooth-proper cohomological family, and let $P_i(T)\in\mathbf Z[T]$ be
the integral Frobenius factor with $P_i(0)=1$ and
$P_i^{(\ell)}=P_{i,\ell}$ for every $\ell\neq p$. For $0\leq i\leq2d$
let $b_i=\deg P_i$ be the Betti number, and let

$$
\chi=\sum_{i=0}^{2d}(-1)^ib_i
$$

be the Euler characteristic. Then the integer $d\chi$ is even: there
is an integer $h$ with $d\chi=2h$.

source.place: Proposition prop:functional-equation-parity (Parity of the functional-equation exponent), lines 3486-3494, whose uses are def:smooth-proper-datum, prop:duality-reciprocity, def:euler-characteristic; the registry comment at line 3521 says it 'supplies integrality of the exponent' of def:functional-equation-sign. On master the claim is the remark 'Assume dχ is even; in geometric applications this follows from the duality relations ...' inside def-weil-functional-equation-sign (literature/blueprint/master/blueprint/sec-zeta-weil/sk-thm-fe/def-weil-functional-equation-sign.md) and is argued inline, with no node, in step 2 of sk-thm-fe/prop-functional-equation.md and step 2 of sk-thm-weil5/thm-weil-final-functional-equation.md. Human source of the functional equation whose exponent dχ/2 it makes an integer: Milne, Lectures on Étale Cohomology v2.21 (literature/milne-lectures-on-etale-cohomology_LEC.pdf), §27, Theorem 27.12 and Remark 27.13, pp. 158-159, which writes q^{dχ/2} without stating the parity.

proof.text: *Step 1 (the data, for one fixed prime $\ell$).* Choose a prime $\ell\neq p$ (one of the primes $2,3$ is different from $p$). The finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ and $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ are those of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], and the hypotheses on $X_0$ are those of [def-weil-geometric-hypotheses]. For this $\ell$, $(V_{i,\ell},F_{i,\ell},P_{i,\ell})_{0\leq i\leq2d}$, with $V_{i,\ell}=H^i(X,\Ql)$ and $P_{i,\ell}(T)=\det(1-TF_{i,\ell}\mid V_{i,\ell})$, is the smooth-proper cohomological family of [def-weil-smooth-proper-cohomological-family]. The polynomials $P_i\in\mathbf Z[T]$ of the statement are integral Frobenius factors [def-weil-integral-frobenius-factor] with $P_i(0)=1$ and $P_i^{(\ell')}=P_{i,\ell'}$ for every prime $\ell'\neq p$, so in particular $P_i^{(\ell)}=P_{i,\ell}$ for the chosen $\ell$: they are exactly the polynomials that [prop-duality-reciprocity] takes as its $P_i$ for this $\ell$. The integers $b_i=\deg P_i$ are the Betti numbers of [def-weil-betti-numbers], which are also the $b_i=\deg P_i$ of [prop-duality-reciprocity], and $\chi=\sum_{i=0}^{2d}(-1)^ib_i$ is the Euler characteristic of [def-weil-determinant-constants], defined there by the same formula.

source.place: Proposition prop:functional-equation-parity, lines 3486-3494 ('For every smooth-proper datum ... the integer $d\chi$ is even'; uses def:smooth-proper-datum, prop:duality-reciprocity, def:euler-characteristic); no proof in the source

proof.text: *Step 2 (the duality relations).* By [prop-duality-reciprocity], applied to $X_0$, the prime $\ell$ of Step 1 and these $P_i$: (i) $b_i=b_{2d-i}$ for every integer $i$ with $0\leq i\leq2d$; (ii) if $d$ is odd, then $b_d$ is even (its last clause, which rests on the middle-degree pairing being alternating and on [lem-weil-alternating-form-dimension], step 6 of that node's proof).

source.place: proof, lines 117-120: 'These same reciprocity relations show that $d\chi$ is even ... If $d$ is odd, then [prop-duality-reciprocity] gives that $b_d$ is even'

proof.text:
*Step 3 (pairing $i$ with $2d-i$).* By (i) of Step 2, the integers $b_0,\ldots,b_{2d}$ satisfy $b_i=b_{2d-i}$ for all $0\leq i\leq2d$, so [lem-weil-symmetric-alternating-sum-parity] gives

$$
\chi=2S+(-1)^db_d,\qquad S=\sum_{i=0}^{d-1}(-1)^ib_i\in\mathbf Z.
$$

source.place: proof, lines 120-124: 'pairing the terms indexed by $i$ and $2d-i$ gives $\chi=2\sum_{0\leq i<d}(-1)^ib_i+(-1)^db_d$'

proof.text: *Step 4 (conclusion).* If $d$ is even, $d=2e$ with $e\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, and $d\chi=2h$ with $h=e\chi$. If $d$ is odd, then $b_d=2c$ for an integer $c$ by (ii) of Step 2, so by Step 3 $\chi=2S+(-1)^d\cdot2c=2(S-c)$ is even, and $d\chi=2h$ with $h=d(S-c)$. In both cases $d\chi$ is even.

source.place: proof, lines 117-125: 'This is immediate if $d$ is even ... which is even'

split_report.summary: The slopmaster2 LaTeX (lines 3486-3494) states the proposition with no proof; the argument is the inline paragraph of the master proof of prop-functional-equation (lines 117-125), which the node's creator recorded. Wrote it in four steps: fix one prime l != p and identify the data with those of prop-duality-reciprocity (the statement's P_i work for every l, so for this one); take b_i=b_{2d-i} and, for odd d, the evenness of b_d from prop-duality-reciprocity (its step 6, via lem-weil-alternating-form-dimension); the pairing identity chi = 2 sum_{i<d} (-1)^i b_i + (-1)^d b_d, hidden in the source as 'pairing the terms', made into the new node lem-weil-symmetric-alternating-sum-parity (searched in Mathlib: only the primitives Finset.sum_range_reflect, Finset.prod_involution, Int.even_add/even_mul); the case split on the parity of d is elementary. Statement and stmt_deps kept: they are correct against the source and every listed node is used.
